results.root_cause_actual: PR #881 simultaneously raised the payments-svc read timeout from 3s to 30s and disabled the circuit breaker. When the partner acquirer degraded to p99 12.4s at 18:47Z, gateway threads blocked in PaymentsClient.execute() for up to 29.9s each instead of failing fast at 3s. Because the ALB proxy_read_timeout remained at 10s (unchanged since 2024), the ALB closed each client-facing connection after 10s and emitted a 504, but the gateway worker thread continued holding the upstream connection for the remaining ~20s. The combination of 30s thread occupancy per slow payment request and a fixed pool of 64 shared worker threads caused pool saturation (64/64 busy, accept queue depth 611), starving all gateway routes — including /v1/orders and /v1/catalog which never touch payments-svc — and dropping gateway availability to 88.1%.
results.root_cause_expected: PR #881 raised the gateway's payments-svc read timeout from 3s to 30s (and disabled the circuit breaker) while the edge load balancer's proxy_read_timeout stayed at 10s. When partner latency rose, the edge cut clients off at 10s with 504s while gateway worker threads stayed pinned on the upstream call for the full 30s, saturating the 64-thread pool and taking down routes that never touch payments-svc.

judge.reason: Both identify the same underlying cause: PR #881's mismatch between the raised payments-svc timeout (3s→30s) and the unchanged ALB timeout (10s), combined with circuit breaker disablement, causing thread pool saturation when partner latency increased.

mechanism: PR #881 (commit 3f0ab155) raised PAYMENTS_READ_TIMEOUT from 3s to 30s and disabled the circuit breaker for payments-svc, deployed at 18:40:00Z
At 18:47Z the partner acquirer p99 latency spiked from 1.9s to 12.4s (known degradation, ticket ACQ-3391)

Under the old 3s timeout + circuit breaker, these slow calls would have failed fast; under the new 30s timeout with no circuit breaker, gateway threads block in PaymentsClient.execute() for up to 30s per request

The ALB proxy_read_timeout remained at 10s; ALB closes the client-facing connection after 10s and emits a 504, but the gateway thread is still holding the upstream payments-svc connection open for the remaining ~20s
Each slow payment request ties up one gateway thread for ~30s instead of ~3s, multiplying thread occupancy by ~10x
With only 64 worker threads, the pool saturates (64/64 busy, accept queue depth 611) as threads pile up waiting on slow acquirer responses
All routes on the gateway — including /v1/orders and /v1/catalog which never touch payments-svc — are starved of threads, returning 504s, dropping gateway availability to 88.1%

ruled_out.candidate: Partner acquirer degradation (p99 12.4s) as sole root cause
ruled_out.why_not: Under v9.1.7 the same acquirer slowness would have triggered 3s timeouts and circuit breaker trips, failing fast without saturating threads. The acquirer degradation is a necessary co-trigger but only became catastrophic because PR #881 removed both defenses. payments-svc itself remained healthy (5xx 0.03%, CPU 34%).

ruled_out.candidate: ALB proxy_read_timeout mismatch (10s) as root cause
ruled_out.why_not: The ALB timeout has been 10s since 2024 and was not changed by this release. It contributes to the symptom (ALB closes client connections before gateway threads finish), but the mismatch only became harmful because PR #881 extended the gateway-side timeout to 30s, making threads hold connections far beyond 10s. The ALB config itself did not change.

ruled_out.candidate: Thread pool size (64 threads) as root cause
ruled_out.why_not: The thread pool was unchanged at 64. Before this deploy, threads_busy was 9/64 with no incident. The pool size is a capacity constraint that made saturation occur faster, but the cause of threads being consumed for 30s instead of 3s is the timeout change, not the pool size.

red_herrings.why_not: 2026-08-23T18:56:02.339Z INFO  api-gateway payments-svc itself: 5xx rate 0.03%, cpu 34%, healthy — payments-svc was healthy throughout; the slowness originated at the partner acquirer, not payments-svc.
PAYMENTS_CONNECT_TIMEOUT  1s  -> 1s      (unchanged) — connect timeout was not altered; it plays no role in thread blocking once a connection is established.
GATEWAY_WORKER_THREADS    64  -> 64      (unchanged) — thread count was not changed; it is a capacity constraint but not the cause of threads being held for 30s.
